name: Zara Kang
life: “I still remember my wife jumping a puddle in her interview shoes.” People around the steps at Pier Beach know Zara by a small Saturday habit. Zara watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: My wife stepped between the rungs laughing. It's the first time I've seen her laugh in town since our son left.
appearance: Zara has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a plum-colored cardigan with a narrow brass watch set a little fast. In conversation Zara presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Zara feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To let the family keep the memory of the laugh.
family: Anton Long is Zara’s cousin raised in the same household. Zara picks the meeting place. Anton sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A shelf of apologies*, Anton says, “I spilled coffee on page six and copied the page by hand.”
connections: Cory Stahl. The family playing among the rungs moves aside for a crossing signal somebody can hear.

reactions.situation: A driver sounds a horn halfway through the crossing
reactions.response: Zara asks for a pause until the people carrying the ladder can clear the crossing safely.
